newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sees bright prospects for gas sector in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sees bright prospects for gas sector in 1997.

text.p: Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi has said he expects Egypt's gas sector to grow in 1997 with more foreign investment and the development of new projects.

"There will be new impetus in Egypt's natural gas sector in 1997. The new year will also witness more interest in protecting the environment than ever before...(and) entry into a new stage in petrochemicals," Banbi was quoted on Monday as saying.
His interview on the 1997 outlook for Egypt's gas sector was published in the government newspaper al-Akhbar.
"The new year will see international tenders to explore for oil and gas in Egypt in seven regions. It is expected the tenders will see a new international response," Banbi said.
He said two of them were in the West Mediterranean region with a total area of 37,000 square km (14,300 square miles), four in the Western Desert and one in the Eastern Desert.

This month Banbi told Reuters that Egypt had awarded 13 concession agreements in 1996 to international companies, bringing commitments to drill about 82 exploratory wells and expenditure of $295 million.
He said he expected about 10 concessions awarded in 1997.
"But the activity will be more than in 1996 because we will be exploring and developing previous discoveries that have been found during 1995 and 1994," he said.
Foreign companies play a large role in energy exploration and development in Egypt, where natural gas production was about 1.31 billion cubic feet (37 million cubic metres) per day in October.
Banbi said in 1997 Egypt's gas distribution to homes and industries would be extended and projects implemented to set up two units to process lead-free or low lead petrol.
Last month Egypt announced major plans to export gas to Turkey with the U.S. oil company Amoco.
"Discussions are kicking into high gear on that," Bob Miles, Amoco Egypt's exploration manager, told Reuters by telephone.

Under a memorandum of understanding with Turkey's state Botas, Egypt is to export to Turkey up to 10 billion cubic metres (353 billion cubic feet) of liquefied natural gas a year by the year 2000. The project will cost between $2 billion and $4 billion.
Amoco announced recent gas discoveries in the Nile Delta and Miles said Amoco has "reasonably firm" plans for 12 exploratory wells in the Nile Delta.
It is also hoping to develop some of its leases and is continuing feasibility studies to develop finds it already has.
"In 1997 we do have big plans. There is no doubt there is increased focus on the Nile Delta," Miles said.
"The pace of exploration will continue very aggressively. We hope to see feasibility studies turn into firm development plans to supply both export markets and domestic gas needs," he said.
"We don't yet have a discovery on our 100 percent leases but we are currently drilling a well on offshore North Sinai concession," Miles said.
